summary: I inspected every file named in the Objective Contract and re-derived each defect from source rather than from the reports. B1, B2, B4(schema claim not re-run), B5, B6, B7, B8, B9 and A-1 all reproduce in the code as described. Three findings change the plan materially. (1) NEW BLOCKING DEFECT, not in either report: `backend/doorway/mutation_check.py` is already red — 4 of its 36 mutation patterns no longer exist in the source they target (three point at the deleted in-memory `_by_token` session store, one at a removed `server.py` line), and the harness scores a not-found pattern as `missed` and exits 1. One of the four also names a test that was deleted in the Phase 2 work. Any package whose acceptance criterion is "the mutation check is green" is unverifiable until this is repaired, so it must be package one. (2) B3's recommended fix as written cannot be implemented: `engine/test_manifest.py:112-125` is a currently-passing test that asserts `checked.coerced == ()` for exactly the "HIGH"/"high"/" High " case B3 wants recorded, and its assertion message states the deliberate reason. That collides head-on with success criterion 6 ("no package requires weakening or deleting an existing passing test"). B3 is therefore an owner decision, not a one-line fix, and the safe reading is that the docstring — not the code — is what is wrong. (3) The "minimal" A-1 fix (actor-scoped RLS on `current_setting('cw.actor') = '__signin__'`) is weaker than the audit presents it: `cw.account.person` has no constraint reserving `__signin__`, and `POST /accounts` (`writes.py:339`) lets an administrator create an account with an arbitrary person string, so an account literally named `__signin__` would satisfy the policy; and the literal `"__signin__"` is hard-coded five times in `sessions.py` instead of imported from `identity.LOOKUP_ACTOR`, so putting it in SQL creates a second (really a seventh) copy of one rule — which hard constraint 3 forbids. On evidence, the dedicated lookup role is the correct choice. I propose nine single-owner packages, sequenced so that no two mutate the same file concurrently.

diagnosis: Observed — B1 is a layering gap, not a classification bug. server.py:285 rules on the shape of the whole body; nothing rules on the shape of a field. refusals.classify sees the consequence (a driver ProgrammingError with sqlstate None) and, correctly by its own design, treats an unrecognised psycopg.Error as the service's fault. Both files are behaving as written; the rule was simply never written at the field level.

Inferred — Because three modules bind parameters outside Write.bind (executions.py, runs.py, manifests.py), a boundary-only fix leaves holes and a classify-only fix produces a message the caller cannot act on. The two proposals in the bug report are complements, not alternatives: classify is the floor that covers every present and future bind site, Write.bind is the ceiling that names the field.

Observed — B2 is a transaction-scope defect with a concurrency consequence. Nothing between the read at advisory.py:281 and the insert at 306 requires atomicity: the insert's inputs are all in local variables, and the module defines its own output as advisory.

Inferred — Splitting the transaction introduces a real time-of-check/time-of-use gap: the ticket's visibility was decided by policy in transaction one and the insert happens in transaction two. The insert's own policy still governs it, so the gap is a staleness gap rather than an authorisation gap, but the package must say so rather than discover it.

Observed — B3 is a documentation defect masquerading as a code defect. The code, the mutation harness and a passing test with a written rationale all agree that a case variant of High is not a 'rewrite'. Only the docstring's phrase 'every real rewrite' disagrees. The bug report's probe reproduces the intended behaviour and reads it as the defect.
Observed — B4 is correctly characterised: the invariant holds and is enforced by prose in documents.py:47-56. The gap is that nothing executable asserts it.

Observed — B5 is a coupling that is true today and undocumented. Both sites rebuild `reasons` by re-asking the category map to fail, so the list is non-empty only while 'dropped' and 'UnknownCategory' remain the same condition.

Observed — B6 is a consistency defect, not a vulnerability: every one of the six event values is a module-local literal. Its cost is that it teaches the wrong pattern in a codebase that spends ten lines at db.py:196 explaining why even a fixed role name is composed safely.
Observed — B7 is latent and correctly diagnosed. The trap is that `required` and `required_if` read as though they compose.

Observed — B9's diagnosis is right but incomplete. It names two cluster-wide statements; there is a third, `grant cw_viewer, … to cw_app` at 0016:45, which writes pg_auth_members on every rebuild and is equally unguarded. A retry-once wrapper around only the two named statements would leave a smaller version of the same collision.

Observed — A-1 is exactly as reported. The migration's header calls cw_viewer 'the lookup role' and that sentence is true on the sign-in path and false everywhere else, which is the same failure class 0031's header was written about.

Observed — NEW: the doorway mutation harness is red in the working tree and neither report noticed. Four checks silently stopped guarding anything when the Phase 2 work replaced the in-memory session store, and the harness's design — a not-found pattern counts as unguarded and fails the run — means the repository's own verification gate is currently failing for reasons unrelated to any of B1–B9.

Inferred — This is the same failure the audit's C-2 describes (a guard test that reached main red), one layer up: a guard harness that reached the working tree stale. It is worth saying in the plan because the repository has now produced this failure twice in three days.
symptoms: Observed — A caller who sends `{"counterparty": {"nested": [1,2]}}` to POST /deals receives HTTP 500 'the service failed'; the same endpoint returns HTTP 400 for a scalar of the wrong type.

Observed — During an advisory call a database connection sits IDLE IN TRANSACTION for up to TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 20 (advisory.py:74); with the pool's default max_size=10, ten concurrent calls exhaust it and later requests fail with 'the service could not reach its database'.
Observed — POST /manifests/check and POST /runs report "coerced": [] for a manifest whose severities were case-normalised.
Observed — Five tables (snapshot, snapshot_ladder_rung, snapshot_member, ruleset, ruleset_member) carry no row-level security; no test asserts the invariant that keeps them unreachable.
Observed — `python doorway/mutation_check.py` prints SKIP for four checks and returns 1, so any gate that runs it is failing today.
Observed — A viewer-role account can `select` every live session token and `delete` all of them (audit probe output quoted at audit_results.md:34-39).

Observed — A full doorway suite run overlapping any other pytest process can error with `psycopg.errors.InternalError_: tuple concurrently updated / CONTEXT: SQL statement "alter role cw_app noinherit"` in an unrelated test.
Observed — app.py:134-139 explains current behaviour with a reason (monotonic clock) that sessions.py:76-78 made untrue.
consequences: Observed — B1 destroys the signal value of the 500 status across every write endpoint: a genuine outage is now indistinguishable in the log from a mistyped form field. This is the specific failure server.py:472-478 and documents.py:12-14 were written to prevent.

Inferred — B2 turns a slow third-party model provider into a total product outage — sign-in included — and points the on-call person at a healthy PostgreSQL. The blast radius is the whole service, not the advisory endpoint.

Observed — The stale mutation checks mean three guarantees about session expiry and sweeping are currently unguarded while the harness's own summary line still reports a count. That is precisely the 'a count that reads as protection' failure the harness's comment at line 455 says it exists to prevent.

Inferred — Fixing B3 as literally recommended would require deleting or weakening test_high_is_matched_on_meaning_not_spelling, which would trade a cosmetic reporting improvement for the loss of the regression guard protecting against silent High-to-Standard downgrades — the exact defect the comment at manifest.py:116-123 records as already having happened once.

Inferred — Adopting A-1's minimal fix would leave a bypass reachable by any administrator (create an account named `__signin__`) and would put a seventh copy of the `__signin__` literal into SQL, where drift from the Python copies is invisible until a session silently stops working.

Observed — B9 keeps producing mystery failures while several sessions work this repository at once, and it also degrades the doorway mutation harness, whose comment records five of six lanes failing from the same cause.
Inferred — B4 costs nothing today and costs a cross-tenant read the first time anyone adds a snapshot-by-id endpoint, which would pass review because the tables look ordinary.
proposed_actions: WP-A (must be first, blocking) — Repair the stale mutation checks. Owner file: backend/doorway/mutation_check.py (plus, if a replacement guard is needed, backend/doorway/test_sessions.py). Repoint the three sessions.py mutations at the database-backed implementation (delete-before-lookup at sessions.py:114, the sweep at 93, the expiry predicate), drop or repoint the one naming the deleted test_an_entry_removed_mid_check_is_no_session_not_a_crash, and repoint 'the query selector is discarded before it reaches the app' at its current server.py line. Rationale for going first: the harness returns 1 today, so no later package can honestly claim 'verify is green'. Acceptance: the pattern-existence probe reports 0 stale for both harnesses, and the doorway harness exits 0.

WP-B (B1 + B7; single owner of writes.py and refusals.py) — Two complementary guards. In refusals.classify add a branch before the catch-all at refusals.py:100: a psycopg.ProgrammingError carrying sqlstate None never reached the database and is a 400 'rejected'. In Write.bind, refuse a dict or list for any Field not declared as_json=True, naming the field. In the same package fix B7: `demanded = spec.required or (…)`. Add one mutation entry per new guarantee to doorway/mutation_check.py (sequenced after WP-A). Rationale for doing both halves: three modules bind outside Write.bind, so classify is the floor; Write.bind is what makes the message actionable. Goes first among product fixes because several other packages' error paths run through classify.

WP-C (B1 residual) — Enumerate and close the raw bind sites. Owner files: backend/doorway/executions.py, runs.py, manifests.py. The bug report names two modules; manifests.py:99 also passes an unvalidated body value onward. Route these through the same shape guard rather than writing a second copy of it — export one helper from writes.py and call it, so the rule has one home (hard constraint 3). Must be sequenced after WP-B because it consumes WP-B's helper.

WP-D (A-1 + D-1; approval-sensitive, surface for owner decision) — Recommend the dedicated lookup role, not the actor-scoped policy, on evidence: (i) cw.account.person has no reserved-name constraint and POST /accounts takes the person from the body, so an account named `__signin__` would satisfy `current_setting('cw.actor') = '__signin__'`; (ii) the literal is already duplicated five times in sessions.py rather than imported from identity.LOOKUP_ACTOR, and putting it in SQL adds a copy across a language boundary. Create cw_lookup as a seventh, non-application database role; grant cw.session to it alone; revoke from cw_viewer; add 'lookup' to ROLE_TO_DB_ROLE or give Database a dedicated as_lookup() entry point; change LOOKUP_ROLE in identity.py; replace the five literals with the imported constant. Ship with the D-1 boundary test (sign somebody in, then select cw.session as an ordinary viewer, assert zero rows and assert the delete is refused). Migration decision, to be approved: edit 0032 in place rather than adding 0033, because `git status` shows 0032 is untracked and therefore never committed or deployed — forward-only numbering protects applied migrations, and this one has not been applied.

WP-E (B2) — Split the advisory transaction. Owner file: backend/doorway/advisory.py. Transaction one reads the ticket and the two texts and closes; the model call runs with no connection held; transaction two performs the insert. State explicitly in the package that this introduces a staleness window (the ticket could be re-decided between the two transactions) and that the insert's own policy remains the authorisation control. Add the belt-and-braces cap — a semaphore or a small dedicated pool for the advisory path — as a named, separately-testable second deliverable so it can ship even if the split slips.

WP-F (B9) — Stop rewriting cluster-wide role state per test. Owner files: backend/doorway/setup.py, backend/db/migrations/0016_doorway_login.sql, backend/doorway/conftest.py. Prefer the 'assert, do not re-apply' shape the repository already uses at setup.py:44-52: the test harness should verify cw_app's login/noinherit/membership and fail loudly if absent, leaving role maintenance to installation. Note in the package that the diagnosis must cover three statements, not two — `grant cw_viewer, … to cw_app` at 0016:45 is a third unconditional cluster-wide write. Second beneficiary: doorway/mutation_check.py:445-455 documents this exact collision degrading its lanes.

WP-G (B5 + B6; single owner of runs.py, manifests.py, executions.py) — Guard reasons[0] at all four occurrences (both sites use it twice), and pass the audit event as a bound parameter (`select cw.audit(%(event)s, …)`); cw.audit's first parameter is declared text at 0001_foundation.sql:329, so no cast is needed. Bundled because they touch the same three files and must not be edited concurrently.

WP-H (B4) — Add the executable invariant. Owner file: a new test in backend/doorway/. For each of the five unprotected tables, assert that a caller-supplied identifier cannot reach it except through cw.run. Test-only and additive, so it can run in parallel with anything except WP-D. Investigate, and record the answer, whether the five tables can carry policies scoped through cw.run — if they can, that is the better fix and this test becomes its guard.

WP-I (B8 + audit item 7) — Documentation and tidy. Owner files: backend/doorway/app.py (correct the stale monotonic-clock rationale at 134-139 without touching the returned value, which is mutation-guarded at mutation_check.py:186-189), backend/doorway/sessions.py (remove the unused `threading` import at line 32; add `from doorway.db import Database` — verified not to create a cycle, since db.py imports nothing from sessions.py).

WP-J (B3; approval-sensitive, do NOT implement as written) — Escalate rather than code. Present the owner with the conflict: engine/test_manifest.py:112-125 asserts and justifies the current behaviour, so 'record whenever severity != risk.severity' cannot land without weakening a passing test, which success criterion 6 forbids. Recommended resolution on evidence: amend the docstring at manifest.py:96 so 'every real rewrite' says what the code and the test both already mean (a change of severity LEVEL, not of spelling), and leave the code alone. If the owner instead wants case normalisation reported, it must be a distinct field, not the `coerced` set, so the existing guard survives. Either way the package must also update engine/mutation_check.py:256 if manifest.py's else-branch text changes, because the engine harness is currently 0-stale and a source edit would break it.

Cross-cutting, per CLAUDE.md line 6 — Every package's definition of done includes one memory.md record stating the decision and its rationale. Name it as a deliverable rather than an afterthought, because in this repository a fix without its rationale record is incomplete.

Sequencing — WP-A first (unblocks verification). Then WP-B, then WP-C (consumes WP-B). WP-D, WP-E, WP-F, WP-G, WP-H, WP-I are independent of each other and may run in parallel once WP-B has landed, except that WP-D and WP-I both touch sessions.py and must be sequenced (WP-D first, since it changes more of the file). WP-J is a decision, not an edit, and can be raised immediately.

assumptions: Assumed — The four stale mutation patterns became stale in the uncommitted Phase 2 work rather than earlier. Basis: three of them reference `self._by_token`, which the Phase 2 change removed, and sessions.py is listed as modified in git status. I did not run git log on the harness to confirm the exact commit.

Assumed — The doorway mutation harness is what `npm run verify` invokes. Basis: bug_report.md:244 states 'npm run verify runs this suite'. I could not read package.json — it is absent or empty at the repository root — so the wiring is not directly Observed.

Assumed — Splitting the advisory transaction does not break any currently-passing advisory test. Basis: the audit reports advisory.py as the best-tested module in the repository; I read the endpoint but not test_advisory.py in full.
Assumed — B4's list of five unprotected tables is accurate. Basis: quoted pg_class output in bug_report.md. I did not re-run the query against a live PostgreSQL.
Assumed — Creating a seventh database role is acceptable in this phase. It is larger than the alternative and the owner may prefer to defer it; the package surfaces it rather than deciding it.

Inferred — `standard` rigor is proportionate given the deliverable is a plan, but two of the ten items (A-1 and B3) are genuinely approval-sensitive and should not be adjudicated by the integrator alone.
unresolved_questions: Unresolved — Does the owner consider a case-variant severity normalisation a 'rewrite' that belongs in `coerced`? The code, the test and the mutation harness say no; the docstring says yes. Nothing can be safely implemented for B3 until this is answered.

Unresolved — Is `npm run verify` in fact wired to both mutation harnesses? package.json could not be read at the repository root, so the true blast radius of the four stale checks is inferred from bug_report.md rather than observed.

Unresolved — When did the four mutation checks go stale, and did they go stale on committed `main` or only in the working tree? This determines whether WP-A is a repair of committed state or of uncommitted state.

Unresolved — For WP-D, should the new lookup role be a member of nothing at all, or should cw_app gain membership of it? cw_app is granted the six application roles at 0016:45; a seventh role needs the same treatment or sign-in will fail, and that is a migration detail the package must settle.

Unresolved — For WP-E, is any consumer relying on the advisory read and write being atomic? I traced the endpoint's own code and found none, but I did not search callers of cw.advisory_assessment across the SQL layer.

Unresolved — For WP-H, can the five snapshot/ruleset tables carry policies scoped through cw.run at all, or does the pinned-library read path require unscoped access? The answer decides whether the package is a test or a migration.

Unresolved — Whether the concurrent session committing to `main` (contract assumption A5) will touch any of the eleven owner files. Two commits landed during the preceding audit; the packages should be written to rebase cleanly.
risks: High — Implementing B3 as the bug report recommends deletes a regression guard against silent High-to-Standard downgrades, the exact defect manifest.py:116-123 records as having already happened once. Mitigation: WP-J escalates rather than edits.

High — Any package that edits a mutation-targeted source string without updating the corresponding harness entry turns a green check into a silent SKIP, which the harness scores as unguarded. Four such strings already went stale this way. Mitigation: every package's checklist includes 're-run the stale-pattern probe for both harnesses'.

Medium — Adopting A-1's minimal actor-scoped policy would ship a fix with a known administrator-reachable bypass (an account named `__signin__`) and a rule copied across the Python/SQL boundary, violating hard constraint 3. Mitigation: WP-D recommends the dedicated role and states the evidence.

Medium — WP-B's Write.bind guard is exactly the kind of change that invites a wording assertion. CLAUDE.md records five failures from that in one day. Mitigation: acceptance criteria assert status 400 and the absence of the 'broke' kind, never the message text.

Medium — WP-E's transaction split creates a time-of-check/time-of-use window. It is a staleness window, not an authorisation hole, but it must be documented in the package rather than discovered in review.
Medium — WP-B, WP-C and WP-D all touch files that other packages also touch (writes.py, sessions.py). Without the stated sequencing, two owners would collide.

Low — WP-F's 'assert rather than re-apply' approach changes what a fresh developer machine needs done before tests run. The package must say how a first-time setup is bootstrapped, or the harness will fail loudly on a clean cluster.
Low — Fixing B1 will change status codes on paths that existing tests may assert as 500. WP-B must enumerate those tests before editing, since criterion 6 forbids weakening them.
acceptance_criteria: WP-A — A script that loads MUTATIONS from both harnesses and checks each find-string against its target file reports 0 stale for backend/doorway/mutation_check.py and 0 for backend/engine/mutation_check.py; `python doorway/mutation_check.py` exits 0. (This probe is executable and was run during planning; its current output is 4 stale and 0 stale respectively.)

WP-B — A request sending a dict or a list as any non-as_json field returns HTTP 400 with body kind != 'broke', asserted on two unrelated endpoints (POST /deals, POST /agreements/execute). A separate unit test asserts refusals.classify(psycopg.ProgrammingError with sqlstate None).status == 400. No test asserts any message text. A field declared required=True and required_if=(...) is still demanded when the condition is false. New mutation entries for both guarantees are caught by their named tests.

WP-C — For each raw-bind endpoint in executions.py, runs.py and manifests.py, a dict-valued field returns 400 rather than 500. A test asserts that the shape guard is imported from one module rather than reimplemented (for example, by asserting the helper's identity or by a grep-style test in the shape the repository already uses for NEVER_FROM_THE_BODY).

WP-D — A test signs a person in, then, as an ordinary viewer, selects from cw.session and asserts zero rows, and attempts a delete and asserts it is refused or affects zero rows; the same test asserts the sign-in path still works end to end. A second test asserts that creating an account whose person collides with the lookup actor does not grant it session access (or that such a name is refused). The migration decision (edit 0032 vs add 0033) is recorded in memory.md with the git evidence that 0032 is unapplied.

WP-E — A test stubs the model call to block, and asserts from an independent connection that zero backends are idle-in-transaction while it blocks. A second test asserts the advisory endpoint cannot occupy more than N pool connections concurrently. All existing advisory tests still pass unmodified.

WP-F — Two pytest processes running the doorway suite concurrently both complete without `tuple concurrently updated`, exercised for the three cluster-wide statements (0016's alter, 0016's grant, setup.py's alter). A test asserts the harness fails loudly if cw_app's noinherit/login/membership are absent, rather than silently repairing them.

WP-G — A test forces checked.dropped to be non-empty with an empty reasons list and asserts the endpoint returns 409 rather than 500.
